problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds, is given by

$$
v=⟨6t+1,-3{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Acceleration for Plane Motion Using Differentiation

feedback.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨3{t}^{3},\,-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=3.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨9{t}^{2},\,-t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(3) & =⟨9(3)^{2},\,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨9\cdot 9,\,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨81,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$
